header.heading: naming the axes a weasel component's look varies along

gloss.lead: The angle a component comes from, its spin or slant: for advanced users, debug output, an aside, a preview, the action that confirms.
items: Today on containers (panels, frames, callouts, dialogs, sidebar sections), and declared but drawing nothing on Button, Badge and Code.
The theme decides how each class looks: fill, border, radius, accent.
Proposed to apply to every component and pass to everything inside a surface that sets it.

gloss.lead: How much an element matters to the reader right now: information, success, a warning, danger.
items: Said six ways today: three separate status types, Toast's tone (warning, error), labkit Toolbar's variant: 'danger', and the danger, notice and important stances.
Independent of what the content is: a debug panel can hold a warning.
Values on the table: info, success, warn, danger.

gloss.lead: How much an element stands out from its neighbors: plain, held back, or picked out in the accent.
items: Today folded into status as neutral, muted and accent, and into Button's primary and secondary.
Proposed to say nothing about meaning or exact color: those are severity and tint.
Open whether it passes to children the way stance does.

roles.title: Tint
roles.was: tone (a palette index or a color)

gloss.lead: A color chosen outright: an index into the theme's palette, or a color value.
items: Today's tone on stance-taking components, Badge's status="custom" with its --badge-edge, and KeyDiagram's per-key tone.
The escape hatch: it wins over severity and tone.
A palette index tells peers apart (series one, two, three); a value sets a color the theme does not know.

gloss.lead: The drawing treatment a component offers: filled or outlined, boxed or bare, with or without chrome.
items: Button: primary, secondary, ghost, link. Badge: solid, outline, subtle. Segmented rows: default, minimal, flat. Select: field, bare.
Per component, because what can be drawn differently depends on the component.
Proposed to carry no meaning and no emphasis: Button's primary is a tone, not a drawing.

roles.title: Motif
roles.description: how a frame draws its heading and edge

gloss.lead: The way a framed group draws its title and border: a title between rules, a tab, a title bar, a plaque, a notch.
items: On MotifFrame and PropertyGroup: rule(), tab(), titlebar(), stereo(), plaque(), notch().
Structure, not color: a motif takes whatever stance, severity and tint the frame has.

gloss.lead: The outline a component is cut to: a pill, a shield, a perforated stamp.
items: Badge's shape and base; its effects layer treatments around that outline.
Independent of the drawing treatment: an outlined shield and a filled shield are one outline.

gloss.lead: The step on the kit's scale a component is set at: its height and its type size together.
items: xs, sm, md on Button, Badge, ToggleBar, Code and most controls.

gloss.lead: How much room a component or a whole interface gives its parts: tight, normal, roomy.
items: Three today: the theme's axis (data-wzl-density), a settings panel's row spacing (tight, normal, roomy), and Slider's track (default, slim), which is thickness rather than room.

gloss.lead: Whether the interface is light on dark or dark on light.
items: Set once on a root as data-wzl-mode: light, dark, auto.

gloss.lead: The complete set of tokens an interface draws from: its colors, type, spacing and stance looks.
items: Set once on a root as data-wzl-theme through applyTheme.

gloss.lead: One of the looks a single theme ships, chosen inside it.
items: Set as data-wzl-variant, a third meaning of the word variant.

gloss.lead: One component drawn in the opposite light from its surroundings: dark keys on a light page.
items: KeyCap's variant="inverse" today.
Local where mode is global: it reverses whatever mode the page is in.

roles.title: Arrangement
roles.description: how a row lays out its parts

gloss.lead: Where a row puts its label and its control, chosen by the kind of control it holds.
items: PropertyRow's variant: default, color, checkbox. Layout, not appearance, filed under the drawing word.

verbs.title: cascade
verbs.description: pass a setting to everything inside

gloss.lead: Give every element inside a surface the setting the surface carries, until one sets its own.
items: Proposed for stance, and possibly severity and tone; never for tint, which belongs to the one element that names it.
Done with CSS custom properties, so it reaches plain HTML and other libraries' components inside the surface.

relations.gloss: an exact color wins; otherwise severity picks the hue, and stance supplies one when neither is set
how strongly that hue shows, separately from which hue it is
how the component is drawn, independent of its color
how big each part is, and how much room sits between them
set once on a root; polarity reverses mode for one component
until a child sets its own

why.title: Why these roles
why.body:
One role per question a component's look answers, read from the props in @weasel-js/ui, labkit and theme on 2026-10-23. Today's words cover these unevenly: variant names four of them, status two, and tone two.

Each role's was line gives the word it has now. Where a role had no word of its own, its key is the name proposed in conversation, so tone and tint open picked.

relations.title: How the axes combine
relations.body: Color comes from four roles in a fixed order of precedence; drawing, scale and the root-level look are each a product of independent roles.

sets.title: Consistent sets
sets.body: One column per field, so a column reads as a system.

operations.title: Operations
operations.body: What the kit does with a setting, rather than a setting.

recommendation.title: Where this stands
recommendation.body: Decided in conversation (2026-10-23): severity is its own axis, apart from stance; tone means how loudly something reads; tint is an exact color and wins over both. Everything else is open, and nothing has been built.
